rca.primary_cause: The gearbox is likely experiencing a fault due to excessive vibration caused by a malfunctioning bearing.
causal_chain: The vibration sensor reading (2.9466) is significantly higher than the normalised baseline value, indicating excessive vibration.
The high vibration is affecting the gearbox, which is a critical component that relies on smooth rotation to function properly.
The excessive vibration is likely caused by a malfunctioning bearing, which is a common root cause of gearbox faults.

recommendation.procedure: Inspect the gearbox for excessive vibration and oil degradation by following the Inspection Procedure outlined in the Gearbox Fault — Inspection & Oil Management document. This includes collecting an oil sample, inspecting the magnetic chip detector, and performing a borescope inspection of gear teeth and the planet carrier. Additionally, check the oil filter differential pressure and inspect the oil cooler for blockage or leakage.
safety_warnings: Wear personal protective equipment (PPE) when working with electrical and mechanical components.
Ensure the turbine is de-energized and locked out before performing any maintenance.

schedule.recommended_action: Perform gearbox inspection and oil management procedure on WTG-003 to diagnose and address the gearbox fault.

parts.supplier_notes: Ensure suppliers can deliver parts within the 2-day deadline.

executive_summary: Turbine WTG-003 has triggered a HIGH risk alert due to a gearbox fault, which is likely caused by a malfunctioning bearing resulting in excessive vibration. This fault poses a significant risk to the turbine's operation and requires immediate attention. We recommend performing a gearbox inspection and oil management procedure within the next 2 days to diagnose and address the issue. This will involve inspecting the gearbox for excessive vibration and oil degradation, and taking corrective action to prevent further damage.
